old_digest: Must not weigh less than five ounces and a half nor more than five ounces and three quarters. It must measure not less than nine inches, nor more than nine inches and one quarter in circumference.
new_digest: The ball must weigh not less than five ounces and a-half, nor more than five ounces and threequarters. It must measure not less than nine inches, nor more than nine and a-quarter inches in circumference.

old_digest: If the bowler shall toss the ball over the striker’s head, or bowl it so wide that in the opinion of the umpire it shall not be fairly within the reach of the batsman, he shall adjudge one run to the parties receiving the innings, either with or without an appeal, which shall be put down to the score of wide balls; such ball shall not be reckoned as one of the four balls; but if the batsman shall by any means bring himself within reach of the ball the run shall not be adjudged.
new_digest: If the bowler shall toss the ball over the striker’s head, or bowl it so wide that in the opinion of the umpire it shall not be fairly within the reach of the batsman, he shall adjudge one run to the party receiving the innings, either with or without an appeal, which shall be put down to the score of wide balls; such ball shall not be reckoned as one of the four balls; but if the batsman shall by any means bring himself within reach of the ball, the run shall not be adjudged.
If the ball shall first touch any part of the striker’s dress or person (except his hands), the umpire shall call “leg bye.”

old_digest: The Striker is Out
If either of the bails be bowled off, or if a stump be bowled out of the ground.
new_digest: The striker is out if either of the bails be bowled off, or if a stump be bowled out of the ground.

old_digest: Or, if in striking, or at any other time while the ball shall be in play, both his feet shall be over the popping crease, and his wicket put down, except his bat be grounded within it.
new_digest: Or, if in striking, or at any other time when the ball shall be in play, both his feet shall be over the popping-crease, and his wicket put down, except his bat be grounded within it;

old_digest: Must not exceed four inches and one quarter in the widest part; it must not be more than thirtyeight inches in length.
new_digest: The bat must not exceed four and a-quarter inches in the widest part; it must not be more than thirty-eight inches in length.

old_digest: Or, if in running the wicket be struck down by a throw, or by the hand or arm, (with ball in hand) before his bat (in hand) or some part of his person be grounded over the popping crease.
new_digest: Or, if in running, the wicket be struck down with a throw, or by the hand or arm (with ball in hand), before his bat (in hand) or some part of his person be grounded over the popping-crease.

old_digest: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket keepers or bowler’s hand, it shall be considered dead: but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the striker at his wicket go outside the popping crease before such actual delivery, the said bowler may put him out, unless (with reference to the 21st law,) his bat in hand, or some part of his person be within the popping crease.
new_digest: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the wicket keeper’s or bowler’s hand, it shall be considered dead; but when the bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the striker at his wicket go outside the popping-crease before such actual delivery, the said bowler may put him out, unless (with reference to the 21st law) his bat in hand, or some part of his person, be within the popping-crease.

old_digest: Must be three in number, twenty-seven inches out of the ground, the bails eight inches in length; the stumps of equal and of sufficient thickness to prevent the ball from passing through.
new_digest: The stumps must be three in number; twentyseven inches out of the ground; the bails eight inches in length; the stumps of equal, and of sufficient thickness to prevent the ball from passing through.

old_digest: If the striker be hurt he may retire from his wicket, and return to it any time during that innings.
new_digest: The striker shall not retire from his wicket and return to it to complete his innings after another has been in, without the consent of the opposite party.

old_digest: If the striker be hurt, some other person may stand out for him, but not go in.

new_digest: No substitute shall in any case be allowed to stand out, or run between wickets for another person, without the consent of the opposite party; and in case any person shall be allowed to run for another, the striker shall be out if either he or his substitute be off the ground in manner mentioned in laws 17 and 21, while the ball is in play.

old_digest: No substitute in the field shall be allowed to bowl, keep wicket, stand at the point, cover the point, or stop behind in any case.
new_digest: In all cases where a substitute shall be allowed, the consent of the opposite party shall also be obtained as to the person to act as substitute, and the place in the field which he shall take.

old_digest: If any fieldsman stop the ball with his hat, the ball shall be considered dead, and the opposite party shall add five runs to their score; if any be run, they shall have five in all.
new_digest: If any fieldsman stop the ball with his bat, the ball shall be considered dead, and the opposite party shall add five runs to their score; if any be run they shall have five in all.

old_digest: The ball having been hit, the striker may guard his wicket with his bat, or with any part of his body except his hands; that the twenty-third law may not be disobeyed.
new_digest: The ball having been hit, the striker may guard his wicket with his bat, or with any part of his body except his hands; that the 23d law may not be disobeyed.

old_digest: The wicket keeper shall not take the ball for the purpose of stumping, until it have passed the wicket; he shall not move till the ball be out of the bowler’s hand: he shall not by any noise incommode the striker; and if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, although the ball hit it, the striker shall not be out.
new_digest: The wicket-keeper shall not take the ball for the purpose of stumping until it has passed the wicket; he shall not move until the ball be out of the bowler’s hand; he shall not by any noise incommode the striker; and if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, although the ball hit it, the striker shall not be out.

old_digest: The umpires in all matches shall pitch fair wickets, and the parties shall toss up for the choice of innings.
new_digest: The umpires in all matches shall pitch fair wickets; and the parties shall toss-up for choice of innings.

old_digest: Must be in a line with the stumps; six feet eight inches in length, the stumps in the centre; with a return crease at each end towards the bowler at right angles.
new_digest: The bowling-crease must be in a line with the stumps; six feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a return crease at each end towards the bowler, at right angles.

old_digest: But if one of the bowler’s feet be not on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease when he shall deliver the ball, the umpire at his wicket unasked must call “No Ball.”
new_digest: But if one of the bowler’s feet be not on the ground behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, when he shall deliver the ball, the umpire at his wicket, unasked, must call “no ball.”

old_digest: No umpire is to be changed during a match, unless with the consent of both parties, except in case of a violation of the 42nd law; then either party may dismiss the transgressor.
new_digest: No umpire is to be changed during a match, unless with the consent of both parties, except in case of violation of the 42d law; then either party may dismiss the transgressor.

old_digest: When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. 2. Laws for Single Wicket. 1.
new_digest: Laws for Single Wicket. 1 When there shall be less than five players on a side, bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. 2.

old_digest: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling stump, and turn before the ball shall cross the play to entitle him to another. 7. The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball stopped with hat; with reference to the 29th & 34th law of double wicket. 8. When there shall be more than four players on a side there shall be no bounds. All hits; byes, and overthrows shall then be allowed. 9. Not more than one minute shall be allowed between each ball. Bets 1. No bet is payable on any match unless it be played out, or given up. 2. If the runs of one player be betted against those of another the bet depends on the firs ...
new_digest: After the striker shall have made one run, if he start again he must touch the bowling-stump, and turn before the ball cross the play, to entitle him to another. 7. The striker shall be entitled to three runs for lost ball, and the same number for ball stopped with bat, with reference to the 28th and 33rd laws of double wicket. 8. When there shall be more than four players on a side, there shall be no bounds: all “hits,” “byes,” and “overthrows” will then be allowed. 9. No more than one minute shall be allowed between each two balls.

old_digest: Must be four feet from the wicket, and paralleled to it; unlimited in length, but not shorter than the bowling crease.
new_digest: The popping-crease must be four feet from the wicket, and parallel to it, unlimited in length, but not shorter than the bowling-crease.

old_digest: Must be pitched opposite to each other by the umpires at the distance of twenty-two yards.
new_digest: The wickets must be pitched opposite to each other by the umpires, at the distance of twentytwo yards.

old_digest: It shall not be lawful for either party during a match, without the consent of the other, to alter the ground by rolling, watering, covering, mowing or beating. This rule is not meant to prevent the striker from beating the ground with his bat near to the spot where he stands during the innings, nor to prevent the bowler from filling up holes with saw dust, &c. when the ground shall be wet.
new_digest: It shall not be lawful for either party during a match without the consent of the other, to alter the ground by rolling, watering, covering, mowing, or beating, except at the commencement of each innings, when the ground may be swept and rolled at the request of either party, such request to be made to one of the umpires within one minute after the conclusion of the former innings. This rule is not meant to prevent the striker from beating the ground with his bat near to the spot where he stands during the innings, nor to prevent the bowler from filling up holes with sawdust, &c., when the ground is wet.

old_digest: Shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, and shall bowl four balls before he change wickets: which he shall be permitted to do once only in the same innings.
new_digest: The bowler shall deliver the ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, and shall bowl four balls before he change wickets, which he shall be permitted to do only once in the same innings.
